cases.rationale: Phase 2 explicitly specifies five text messages per day over 14 days, each linking to an experience survey. This supports the claimed frequency and duration.

The authors studied young adults, explicitly leave generalization to additional age groups unresolved, and require manipulation experiments for definitive causal relations. Replace universal causal proof with prediction of declining subjective well-being in this young-adult sample.

The cited discussion says Facebook use predicts declines in both momentary feelings and life satisfaction, reversing the claim of improvement. Describe declines as predictions rather than established causal effects.

The Affect row and Facebook use column contain .14***, not .41. This is the above-diagonal within-person zero-order correlation; the table note defines *** as p<.001. The reverse Facebook Use row/Affect column is .07 and is between-person. Checked original XML headers and exact cell, without rendered visual inspection.
